mainTopic: When an אשם תלוי is brought, how complete its כפרה is, and what יום הכפורים does and does not atone for
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא that allows an אשם תלוי for a doubt about eating נבלה. רבא objects that the חכמים allow it only for sins with כרת and a חטאת, and that רבי אליעזר goes even further by allowing it as a gift. רבי חייא answers, in the name of רבה, that the ברייתא follows the sages who answered בבא בן בוטא: any real doubt is enough. רבא then gives the verse behind each view. Next, a ברייתא says an אשם תלוי does not give a 'complete' כפרה. רב יוסף explains that a חטאת is still owed if the sin becomes known. רבינא explains instead that יום הכפורים can replace the אשם תלוי but not the definite offerings, citing a משנה. The גמרא then looks for the source that יום הכפורים does not cancel a definite חטאת or אשם. רב דימי, אביי and ריש לקיש compare חטאים to פשעים, and after challenges אביי grounds the comparison in the extra word 'כל'. רבי אלעזר shows from 'before ה׳' that יום הכפורים covers a doubtful sin. Finally, רבא begins a new statement about the משנה's first clause, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A provisional guilt offering for doubtful נבלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that an אשם תלוי is brought for a doubt about eating נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A provisional guilt offering comes for a possible eating of a non-kosher carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling that a person who is unsure whether he ate נבלה brings an אשם תלוי. This ruling is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating נבלה is a plain לאו. It carries no כרת, and doing it by mistake does not require a חטאת. So the ruling extends אשם תלוי to a sin outside the usual חטאת category, and that is what makes it surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; eating it is forbidden
Is brought for (this sin)

phrases.english: A provisional guilt offering comes for the carcass.
phrases.notes: He means a case where a person is not sure whether he ate נבלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with the ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי is brought for a doubt about eating נבלה.

steps.title: The חכמים limit it to sins with כרת and חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects from the משנה: the חכמים say an אשם תלוי comes only for a sin that has כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't we learn in the משנה that the חכמים say one brings a provisional guilt offering only for something whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose accidental violation brings a sin offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling by quoting the חכמים in our משנה, who allow an אשם תלוי only for sins that carry כרת and a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה has no כרת and no חטאת. So by the rule of the חכמים, no אשם תלוי should be possible for it, and the ruling seems to go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing it on purpose is punished with כרת
Doing it by mistake requires a חטאת offering

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't we learn,
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking here, quoting the משנה on this daf.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
phrases.english: And the Sages say: He does not bring a provisional guilt offering
except for a matter whose deliberate violation is כרת
and whose accidental violation is a sin offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an אשם תלוי is brought for נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים require a sin with כרת and חטאת, and נבלה has neither.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר does not fit either
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules out answering with רבי אליעזר, since he allows an אשם תלוי even as a voluntary gift with no doubt at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it follows רבי אליעזר, he holds it can also come as a voluntary gift!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא blocks the obvious answer before anyone can give it. רבי אליעזר's view goes much further than this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling followed רבי אליעזר, there would be no reason to mention a doubt about נבלה at all. רבי אליעזר lets a person bring an אשם תלוי any day as a gift. So the ruling seems to fit neither side of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary gift offering
Also
Comes / can be brought

phrases.english: And if it is רבי אליעזר,
it comes also as a gift!
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says a person may bring an אשם תלוי whenever he wants, even with no doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, בִּנְדָבָה נָמֵי אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by closing off the other opinion in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the ruling follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's view is broader than the ruling, so mentioning a specific doubt like נבלה would not make sense under his view.

steps.title: It follows the sages who answered בבא בן בוטא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that רבה already explained it: the ruling follows the sages who told בבא בן בוטא to wait for a real doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why didn't you learn this? Many times I taught it before the Master, that is רבה, and he told me: Whose view is this? It is the side of רבי אליעזר's discussion, the view of those who spoke to him, as we learned: 'Rather they say to him: wait until you come into a situation of doubt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא is a little surprised that רבא does not know the answer. He reports that רבה explained the ruling follows the sages in the משנה who told בבא בן בוטא to wait until he had a real doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those sages turn down a purely voluntary אשם תלוי, so the ruling is not רבי אליעזר's own view. But they did not limit it to sins with כרת: any real doubt is enough, even a doubt about נבלה. This creates a third view that fits the ruling exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: You learn/teach (it this way)
Many times
Whose opinion is this?
Of those who said to him: the sages who replied to בבא בן בוטא
A situation of doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'רבי אליעזר' and 'those who spoke to him.' The ruling is not רבי אליעזר's own gift-offering view. It is the view of the sages in that same part of the משנה who disagreed with the idea of a gift offering.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מַתְנֵית?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason you did not learn?
phrases.notes: Now רבי חייא is answering רבא, asking why he didn't hear this explanation from רבה.

phrases.english: Many times I taught it before the Master,
and who is that? רבה,
and he said to me: Whose is this?
It is רבי אליעזר, of those who said to him,
phrases.notes: He means the sages in the רבי אליעזר section of the משנה, who answered בבא בן בוטא.

phrases.english: as we learned: Rather, they say to him
wait until you enter a situation of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מַתְנֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both parts of the challenge in steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a third opinion in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling has to follow either the חכמים (who require כרת) or רבי אליעזר (who allows a gift offering), and it fits neither.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows the sages who answered בבא בן בוטא. They require a real doubt, but any doubt counts, even one without כרת.

steps.title: The verse behind 'those who spoke to him'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the sages who answered בבא בן בוטא learn from the verse 'which may not be done... and he is guilty' that any sin can bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of those who spoke to him? The verse says: 'which may not be done... and he is guilty.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the verse behind the view that an אשם תלוי comes for any doubtful sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about אשם תלוי speaks generally about doing something the תורה says 'may not be done.' It does not limit this to sins with כרת. So any doubtful sin, such as נבלה, is included.

keyTerms.meaning: (Which) should be done
And he is guilty

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּאָמְרוּ לוֹ?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of those who said to him?
The verse says: 'Which may not be done (unwittingly) and he is guilty.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17. The word in round brackets isn't actually in the פסוק, so the corrected wording leaves it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּאָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view named in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The general wording 'which may not be done' covers any doubtful sin.

steps.title: The חכמים learn from the word מצות
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins to explain the חכמים: they link the word 'מצות' in the אשם תלוי verse to the same word in the regular חטאת verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of the רבנן, who say one brings a provisional guilt offering only for a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose accidental violation brings a sin offering? 'מצות' and 'מצות', from the sin offering for forbidden fat...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains why the חכמים limit אשם תלוי to sins with כרת and a חטאת. He starts a word-link between two verses, and the next step finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מצות' appears in the אשם תלוי verse and also in the verse of the regular חטאת, the classic example being forbidden חלב. Through this word-link, the חכמים teach that אשם תלוי covers only the kind of sin that a חטאת covers: sins with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Commandments; the shared word that links the two verses
The sin offering for eating forbidden fat, the model case of a regular חטאת
Learning one law from another through a shared word in two verses

steps.whatToRemember: Two views: (1) those who spoke to בבא בן בוטא say any real doubt brings an אשם תלוי, based on 'which may not be done.' (2) The חכמים say only a doubt about a sin with כרת and חטאת, based on the shared word 'מצות.'

phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of the Rabbis,
who say: One does not bring a provisional guilt offering

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְשִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת?
phrases.english: except for a matter whose deliberate violation is כרת and whose accidental violation is a sin offering?
'מצוות‎', 'מצוות', from the sin offering of fat,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17 and ויקרא 4:27, where the same word appears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opposing view, the חכמים quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A word-link on 'מצות' ties אשם תלוי to the sins that require a regular חטאת.

steps.title: Finishing the word-link: the אשם תלוי comes only for a כרת-level sin
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה from 'מצות' is completed. Just as the regular חטאת is for a sin with כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, the אשם תלוי is for the same kind of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there, it is a sin that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, so too here, it is a matter that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation that רבא started in the last step. It spells out what the shared word 'מצות' teaches us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The regular חטאת verse is clearly about sins that bring כרת when done on purpose. Because both verses use the same word, the חכמים carry that limit over to the אשם תלוי. That is the source for the משנה's rule from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too here. The standard wording for a גזירה שוה.
When done on purpose, the punishment is כרת.
When done by mistake, one brings a חטאת.

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, an אשם תלוי comes only for a doubt about a sin whose זדון is כרת and whose שגגה is a חטאת. They learn this from the shared word 'מצות'.

phrases.english: Just as there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the verse about the regular חטאת. 'Here' is the verse about the אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: it is something that on purpose brings כרת and by mistake brings a חטאת,
so too here,
it is a matter that on purpose brings כרת and by mistake brings a חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן, שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְשִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גזירה שוה that רבא began in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי comes only for a sin whose זדון is כרת and whose שגגה is a חטאת.

steps.title: A ברייתא: five אשמות atone, but the אשם תלוי's atonement is not complete
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that five אשמות give כפרה, while an אשם תלוי does not give a complete כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Five guilt offerings atone. A doubtful guilt offering does not give a complete atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that compares the five definite אשמות to the אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is unclear. It says the five 'atone' but does not say how fully, and it says the אשם תלוי gives no 'complete' atonement. The next step asks what this really means.

keyTerms.meaning: The five definite guilt offerings, brought for a sin the person knows he did.
They atone (bring כפרה).
A complete, final atonement.

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
Five guilt offerings atone,

phrases.aramaic: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֵין מְכַפֵּר כַּפָּרָה גְּמוּרָה.
phrases.english: a doubtful guilt offering does not atone with a complete atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new subject: how much כפרה the אשם תלוי gives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five אשמות atone. The אשם תלוי does not give a complete כפרה.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since its wording is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask for the meaning of the ברייתא. This sets up two explanations, one from רב יוסף and one from רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about what the words mean, not an attack. It is unclear what 'not a complete atonement' means and how that sets the אשם תלוי apart from the five.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A request to explain unclear wording.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא in step 8 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What contrast is the ברייתא drawing between the five אשמות and the אשם תלוי?

steps.title: רב יוסף: the five atone completely, the אשם תלוי only for now
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the five אשמות give a full, final כפרה. The אשם תלוי does not, because if the person later learns he truly sinned, he must still bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what it means. Five guilt offerings give a complete atonement, and a doubtful guilt offering does not give a complete atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers by adding the word 'complete' to the first half, so both halves are talking about the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five אשמות close the case for good. The אשם תלוי only protects the person while he is unsure. If he later finds out he really did the sin, he still owes a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Introduces a re-reading of a text.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not complete' does not mean the אשם תלוי does nothing. It does protect the person while the doubt remains. It just is not the final word if the sin later becomes certain.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said: This is what it is saying:
Five guilt offerings atone with a complete atonement,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֵין מְכַפֵּר כַּפָּרָה גְּמוּרָה.
phrases.english: and a doubtful guilt offering does not atone with a complete atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether the כפרה is final. The אשם תלוי still leaves a חטאת owed if the sin later becomes known.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reading does not fit רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this reading does not follow רבי אליעזר. He says an אשם תלוי can come even for a doubt about eating נבלה, a sin that has no חטאת at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is not like רבי אליעזר, who said: A doubtful guilt offering comes for eating נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note: according to רב יוסף, this ברייתא cannot follow רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating נבלה never brings a חטאת. So if an אשם תלוי came for it, there would be nothing left to bring later, and that כפרה would be complete. This clashes with the ברייתא's claim that an אשם תלוי is never a complete כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And this does not follow the view of...
An animal that died without proper שחיטה. Eating it is forbidden but brings no כרת and no חטאת.

phrases.english: And this is not in line with רבי אליעזר,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בָּא עַל הַנְּבֵלָה.
phrases.english: who said: A doubtful guilt offering comes for eating נבלה.
phrases.notes: Since נבלה never brings a חטאת, nothing would be owed later, so that אשם תלוי would be a complete כפרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out a result of רב יוסף's reading: which view the ברייתא must follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רב יוסף, the ברייתא does not follow רבי אליעזר, who allows an אשם תלוי for a sin like נבלה.

steps.title: רבינא: something else can replace the אשם תלוי, but not the five
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads the ברייתא differently. Nothing else can do the job of the five אשמות, since they must be brought whenever the sin becomes known. But something else, יום הכפורים, can do the job of the אשם תלוי, so it is not brought afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what it teaches. For the five guilt offerings, nothing else gives their atonement, because when the sin becomes known he brings them. For the doubtful guilt offering, something else does give its atonement, because when it becomes known he does not bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second, different answer to 'what is it saying'. He says the ברייתא is asking whether something else can take the offering's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבינא, the point is not whether a later חטאת is owed. The point is whether another thing can replace the offering. The five can never be replaced. The אשם תלוי can be replaced by יום הכפורים. Because he does not use רב יוסף's reasoning, the problem with רבי אליעזר does not come up.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches. Introduces a re-reading of the ברייתא.
Nothing else gives their atonement.
It becomes known to him.

phrases.english: רבינא said: This is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה אֲשָׁמוֹת – אֵין אַחֵר מְכַפֵּר כַּפָּרָתָן,
phrases.english: The five guilt offerings: nothing else gives their atonement,
phrases.notes: 'Something else' here means יום הכפורים, as the משנה in the next step shows.

phrases.english: since when it becomes known to him, he brings them.
The doubtful guilt offering: something else gives its atonement,
since when it becomes known to him, he does not bring it,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets, לֵיהּ ('to him'), and some don't. The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 9, different from רב יוסף's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether something else, יום הכפורים, can replace the offering. It can replace the אשם תלוי but not the five.

steps.title: Support from the משנה: יום הכפורים frees one from the אשם תלוי only
steps.stepSummary: רבינא backs his reading with a משנה. People who owe a חטאת or a definite אשם must still bring it after יום הכפורים. People who owe an אשם תלוי are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Those who owe sin offerings or definite guilt offerings, and יום הכפורים passed, must bring them after יום הכפורים. Those who owe doubtful guilt offerings are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a משנה as a source for his idea that 'something else' can take the place of the אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that יום הכפורים wipes out the need for an אשם תלוי but not for definite offerings. That is exactly the 'something else' רבינא was talking about. This makes his reading of the ברייתא grounded in an accepted משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite guilt offerings, for a sin known for sure.
That יום הכפורים passed over them before they brought the offering.
Exempt.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the ברייתא. רב יוסף: the אשם תלוי is not final, because a חטאת is still owed if the sin becomes known. רבינא: the אשם תלוי can be replaced by יום הכפורים, but the five definite אשמות cannot.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Those who owe sin offerings and definite guilt offerings
and יום הכפורים passed over them,
must bring them after יום הכפורים.
Those who owe doubtful guilt offerings are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a משנה as the source for רבינא's explanation in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that 'something else', יום הכפורים, can replace the אשם תלוי but not the definite offerings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: after יום הכפורים, definite חטאות and אשמות must still be brought, but those who owe an אשם תלוי are exempt.

steps.title: What is the source that יום הכפורים does not cancel a חטאת or definite אשם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and asks where in the תורה it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches that people who owe a חטאת or a definite אשם must still bring it after יום הכפורים, but people who owe an אשם תלוי are exempt. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה again. It asks for the source of the rule. This sets up the next steps, which will search for a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the משנה was used as proof for רבינא's reading. Now the גמרא studies the משנה itself. Why should יום הכפורים not forgive a sin that still needs a חטאת or a definite אשם? The גמרא wants a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: People who owe a sin offering
Definite guilt offerings, brought when the sin is known for sure
Guilt offerings brought when it is unsure whether a sin happened
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: Those obligated in sin offerings and definite guilt offerings, etc.
It teaches: Those obligated in sin offerings and definite guilt offerings
over whom Yom Kippur has passed
are obligated to bring them after Yom Kippur;
those obligated in provisional guilt offerings are exempt.
From where are these matters known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה that was cited as proof in step 13 and now asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that יום הכפורים does not forgive sins that still need a חטאת or a definite אשם.

steps.title: רב דימי's source: sins are compared to deliberate sins
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, quoting רבי אמי and רבי חנינא, brings a פסוק that lists פשעים next to חטאים. He learns that יום הכפורים forgives only sins that have no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the כהן atones 'from their deliberate sins, for all their sins.' Accidental sins are compared to deliberate sins. Deliberate sins can never be fixed by a קרבן, so יום הכפורים forgives only accidental sins that also have no קרבן. Sins that have a קרבן are not forgiven by it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question with a פסוק about יום הכפורים. He compares two words in it, פשעים and חטאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts פשעים (deliberate sins) and חטאים (accidental sins) side by side. A deliberate sin never has a קרבן. So the חטאים that יום הכפורים forgives must be the same kind: sins with no קרבן. A sin that has a קרבן, like one needing a חטאת, is not covered, and the person still brings the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Deliberate, rebellious sins
Accidental sins
Similar to; compared to
Sins that can be fixed by bringing a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean יום הכפורים forgives nothing accidental. It forgives accidental sins that have no קרבן. It does not replace a קרבן the person already owes.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 16:16 compares חטאים to פשעים, so יום הכפורים forgives only sins that have no קרבן.

steps.title: אביי: that פסוק is about the inside goat only
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that רב דימי's פסוק speaks about the goat whose blood is brought inside, which does not forgive known sins anyway. The שעיר המשתלח, which does forgive known sins, might forgive even sins that have a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That פסוק is written about the goat brought inside, which does not forgive known sins. But the שעיר המשתלח does forgive known sins. Maybe it forgives even sins that have a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב דימי's proof. He says it proves the rule only for one of the יום הכפורים offerings, not for all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inside goat is weaker: it does not forgive sins the person knows about. So it makes sense that it would not cover sins that have a קרבן. The שעיר המשתלח is stronger and forgives known sins. Nothing in רב דימי's פסוק stops it from forgiving sins that have a קרבן, so the משנה's rule is still unproven.

keyTerms.meaning: The יום הכפורים goat whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים
The goat sent away to עזאזל
A known violation, a sin the person knows he did

phrases.english: which does not atone for violations of a known מצוה;
phrases.notes: He means a sin the person knows he did.

phrases.english: but the scapegoat that is sent away,

I could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עַל חֲטָאִים דִּבְנֵי קׇרְבָּן נִינְהוּ מְכַפֵּר!
phrases.english: it atones even for sins that are subject to an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's use of ויקרא 16:16 as the source for all of יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is about the inside goat, which is weaker. The stronger שעיר המשתלח could still forgive sins that have a קרבן.

steps.title: אביי's source: the same comparison in the פסוק about the שעיר המשתלח
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings the פסוק about the confession over the שעיר המשתלח. It also lists פשעים with חטאים, so even this stronger goat does not forgive sins that have a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said the source is this: 'And he shall confess over it all the sins of the children of Israel and all their deliberate sins, for all their sins.' Accidental sins are compared to deliberate sins. Just as deliberate sins have no קרבן, it forgives only accidental sins with no קרבן. The פסוק limited the שעיר המשתלח on purpose, to teach that it does not forgive sins that have a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new source to replace רב דימי's. He uses the same comparison, but from a פסוק about the שעיר המשתלח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His objection was that the stronger goat was not covered. So he finds the פשעים and חטאים comparison in the פסוק about that very goat. If even the שעיר המשתלח, which forgives known sins, does not forgive sins that have a קרבן, then the משנה's rule follows. The next step challenges this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall confess
Iniquities, sins
The פסוק limited it, leaving certain cases out

steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים, even through the שעיר המשתלח, does not forgive a sin that has its own קרבן. That is why a person who owes a חטאת or a definite אשם must still bring it after יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's practical rule. A known obligation to bring a קרבן stays in place after יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: from here:
"And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:21. Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: and all their transgressions, for all their sins";
sins are similar to transgressions:
just as transgressions are not subject to an offering,
so too sins that are not subject to an offering;

phrases.english: but sins that are subject to an offering, it does not atone for.
And the verse limited it in the case of the scapegoat,

phrases.english: to say that it does not atone for sins that are subject to an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב דימי's source in step 16, אביי offers a new source that fixes the gap he pointed out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 16:21 compares חטאים to פשעים in the פסוק about the שעיר המשתלח, so even it does not forgive sins that have a קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe the deliberate sins in the verse do bring an offering
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי asks אביי how he knows the פשעים in the פסוק are sins with no קרבן. Some deliberate sins do bring a קרבן, like the four cases listed in a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said to אביי: How do you know these פשעים are sins that have no קרבן? Maybe they are the kind that do have a קרבן, as the משנה teaches that four people bring a קרבן for a deliberate sin just as for an accidental one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back on אביי's proof from the confession over the שעיר המשתלח. He questions the basic assumption that פשעים means sins with no קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof worked like this: חטאים are compared to פשעים, and פשעים have no קרבן, so the חטאים forgiven here are also ones with no קרבן. רב דימי attacks the middle link. There are four cases where even a deliberate sin brings a קרבן, so maybe the פסוק means exactly those פשעים. If so, the comparison would teach the opposite of what אביי wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: Deliberate, rebellious sins
Sins that require bringing a קרבן
A sin done on purpose
A sin done by accident
Perhaps, maybe

steps.confusionAlert: Normally a deliberate sin does not bring a קרבן; the קרבן is for accidental sins. The four cases in the משנה are the rare exceptions, and that is exactly why רב דימי can use them.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi said to him:

Perhaps these are the kind that do bring an offering,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
Four people bring an offering for a deliberate sin just as for an accidental one.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה earlier in this מסכתא (ט.). It lists cases like a טמא נזיר and certain false oaths.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהָנֵי פְּשָׁעִים לָאו בְּנֵי קׇרְבָּן נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind אביי's proof in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the פשעים in the confession פסוק are sins with no קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some deliberate sins (the four of the משנה) do bring a קרבן, so the פסוק's פשעים might be those. Then the comparison would not exclude sins with a קרבן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns the same rule from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a teaching of רבי יוסי in the name of ריש לקיש. It learns from the confession פסוק that the שעיר המשתלח forgives only sins with no קרבן, because חטאים are compared to פשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוסי and ריש לקיש: 'And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel and all their transgressions, for all their sins.' חטאים are like פשעים. Just as the goat forgives פשעים, which have no קרבן, so it forgives only חטאים that have no קרבן. But חטאים that do have a קרבן, it does not forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that an אמורא from ארץ ישראל made the same derivation as אביי. This gives אביי's reading of the פסוק outside support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש uses the very same comparison: the פסוק puts חטאים next to פשעים, so they share a rule. Because פשעים have no קרבן, the חטאים forgiven by the goat are also only those with no קרבן. This confirms אביי's approach, but it still rests on the assumption רב דימי just questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, compared with
Atones, brings forgiveness
And he shall confess (the כהן גדול over the goat)

phrases.english: It was also stated:
When Ravin came,

phrases.english: "And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel

phrases.english: just as it atones for transgressions, which have no offering,

phrases.english: so too it atones for sins that have no offering,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֲטָאִים דִּבְנֵי קׇרְבָּן – לָא מְכַפַּר.
phrases.english: but sins that have an offering, it does not atone for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an independent אמורא who reads the פסוק the same way as אביי
steps.raayaObject: אביי's derivation that the שעיר המשתלח does not forgive sins that have a קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין quoting רבי יוסי in the name of ריש לקיש on ויקרא 16:21

steps.title: אביי recalls the same challenge against this reading
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he also learned the rule from this פסוק, and רב דימי challenged him with the four deliberate sins that bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I also learned it from this פסוק, and רב דימי challenged me: How do you know these פשעים have no קרבן? Maybe they are the ones that do, as the משנה teaches that four bring a קרבן for a deliberate sin just as for an accidental one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רבין that he had the same reading and faced the same problem. The גמרא repeats רב דימי's challenge, now aimed at ריש לקיש's version too, and sets up רבין's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same question from step 18 now hits ריש לקיש's teaching as well, since it rests on the same assumption. By telling רבין about the challenge, אביי invites him to defend the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged me, raised a difficulty against me
This פסוק

phrases.english: Abaye said:

and Rav Dimi raised a difficulty against me:
From where do we know that these transgressions
are not the kind that bring an offering?
Perhaps those are the kind that do bring an offering,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִתְנַן: אַרְבָּעָה מְבִיאִין עַל הַזָּדוֹן כִּשְׁגָגָה!
phrases.english: as we learned: Four bring an offering for a deliberate sin just as for an accidental one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא נָמֵי מֵהָדֵין קְרָא אָמְרִי וְאַקְשִׁי לִי רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב דימי's challenge to ריש לקיש's identical derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation shared by אביי and ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The four cases show that some פשעים do bring a קרבן, so the comparison might point the other way.

steps.title: Most deliberate sins have no offering
steps.stepSummary: רבין answers that most פשעים have no קרבן, so the פסוק's פשעים should be understood as sins without a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין said to him: Most פשעים do not bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין defends the reading by pointing out that the four cases are rare exceptions. In general, deliberate sins have no קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין's idea is to follow the usual case: the four exceptions should not decide what the word פשעים means in the פסוק. Since the typical פשע has no קרבן, the comparison still teaches that the goat forgives only sins with no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority, most cases

phrases.english: Ravin said to him:
Most transgressions are not the kind that bring an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four cases might show that the פסוק's פשעים are sins with a קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: Those are rare exceptions; most פשעים have no קרבן, so the comparison stands

steps.title: The verse does not say most
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבין's answer: the פסוק says 'all their transgressions', not 'most'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is 'most' written in the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבין's answer. The פסוק does not limit itself to typical cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says כל פשעיהם, all their transgressions, and that includes the four that do bring a קרבן. So a 'most' argument cannot define the פשעים here, and רב דימי's challenge is back in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? Pointing out that the פסוק does not say this

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רבין.

phrases.english: Is "most" written there?
phrases.notes: The פסוק says 'all their transgressions', so it covers even the four that bring a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבין's answer
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the majority answer; אביי gives a new answer in steps 23 and 24
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says all פשעים, not most, so the exceptions cannot be ignored

steps.title: A new start from the beginning of the verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a new answer from the first part of the פסוק. A ברייתא teaches that עוונות means deliberate sins, supported by the פסוק 'עונה בה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It comes from the beginning of the פסוק, 'And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel.' A ברייתא teaches: 'עוונות' means deliberate sins. And similarly it says: 'his iniquity shall be upon him'.
steps.whatsHappening: With the old answer rejected, אביי opens a new approach to רב דימי's question. He starts with the word עוונות at the beginning of the פסוק and proves it means deliberate sins. This lays the groundwork for his full answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines עוונות as זדונות, and backs this with עונה בה, said about someone who sins on purpose. So the פסוק already mentions deliberate sins with its first word. When it then adds 'all their פשעים', which are also deliberate sins, that phrase looks extra. The next step uses this extra phrase to answer רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a new answer after the old one fell
The beginning of the פסוק
Iniquities
Sins done on purpose
And similarly it says, bringing a supporting פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: Defining עוונות as deliberate sins lets אביי read each word of the פסוק as its own category. That is how he hopes to answer רב דימי without relying on 'most'.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It comes from the beginning of the verse:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהִתְוַדָּה עָלָיו אֶת כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: "And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel,"
and it was taught: "Iniquities" are deliberate sins.
And similarly it says: "his iniquity shall be upon him."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:31. It is said about someone who sins on purpose, so עוון means a deliberate sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected majority answer with a new reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק word by word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פשעים might mean the deliberate sins that bring a קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: עוונות already means deliberate sins, so the phrase 'all their פשעים' is extra and can be used for something else (step 24)

steps.title: The extra word 'all' compares sins to transgressions
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his new answer. The extra word 'כל' (all) before פשעים is there only to compare חטאים to פשעים, which teaches that the שעיר המשתלח does not forgive sins that bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And all their transgressions, for all their sins.' Why do I need the word 'all'? It is there to compare sins to transgressions. Just as transgressions are sins with no קרבן, so too the sins it forgives are sins with no קרבן. But sins that do bring a קרבן, it does not forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes the answer he started in the last step. He explains why the פסוק says 'all their transgressions' and what that extra wording teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 showed that עוונות already covers deliberate sins, so the פסוק did not need 'all their פשעים' to tell us that. The extra phrase must be there on purpose, to compare חטאים to פשעים. Since the comparison is deliberate, it follows the typical פשע, which has no קרבן, and the four exceptions from step 18 do not undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare one thing to another so they share the same rule
Transgressions (rebellious sins)
Sins (here, sins done by mistake)
Sins that call for a קרבן to bring atonement
Atones, brings forgiveness

steps.whatToRemember: The שעיר המשתלח forgives only sins that have no קרבן. Sins that call for a קרבן still need their קרבן. אביי learns this from the extra word 'כל' with פשעים, which compares חטאים to פשעים.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 22 אביי rejected רבין's 'most פשעים' argument because the פסוק does not say 'most.' Here the phrase 'כל פשעיהם' is extra, since עוונות already covers deliberate sins. Because it is extra, it is free to teach a comparison between חטאים and פשעים.

phrases.english: "And all their transgressions, for all their sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:21

phrases.english: why do I need "all"?
phrases.notes: Deliberate sins are already covered by עוונות, so the extra 'all their transgressions' seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: to compare [sins] to transgressions:
just as transgressions are not subject to a קרבן,
so too sins that are not subject to a קרבן,
but sins that are subject to a קרבן
it does not atone for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the new answer אביי began in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: an extra word is used to teach a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to פשעים seemed to fail, since some פשעים (the four in the משנה) do bring a קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: Deliberate sins are covered by עוונות. The extra 'כל פשעיהם' compares חטאים to פשעים, so only sins with no קרבן are forgiven by the שעיר המשתלח

steps.title: Source for exempting provisional guilt offerings after יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that people who owe an אשם תלוי are exempt after יום הכפורים, and asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: those who owe an אשם תלוי, and so on. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought when a person is not sure whether he sinned. The משנה says יום הכפורים frees him from bringing it, and the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisional guilt offerings, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Those liable to bring provisional guilt offerings, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שעיר המשתלח discussion to a new clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches יום הכפורים exempts someone from an אשם תלוי

steps.title: יום הכפורים atones for a sin only ה׳ knows about
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings the פסוק 'from all your sins before ה׳'. A sin known only to ה׳, meaning a doubtful sin, is atoned for by יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: the פסוק says 'From all your sins before ה׳.' A sin that nobody knows about except המקום is atoned for by יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question with a פסוק about יום הכפורים. He reads 'before ה׳' as meaning a sin that only ה׳ knows about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of an אשם תלוי, the person himself does not know whether he sinned. Only ה׳ knows. Since יום הכפורים atones for sins 'before ה׳', it covers this doubtful sin, and so the אשם תלוי is no longer needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Before ה׳, read here as a sin known only to ה׳
Literally 'the Place', a name for ה׳
Recognizes, knows about

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason an אשם תלוי falls away after יום הכפורים: it is a doubtful sin, and only ה׳ knows whether it happened.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: the verse states:
"From all your sins before the Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:30

phrases.aramaic: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: a sin that no one is aware of except the Omnipresent
Yom Kippur atones for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Before ה׳' means a sin only ה׳ knows of, which is the doubtful sin of an אשם תלוי. יום הכפורים atones for it.

steps.title: רבא begins a statement about the משנה's first clause
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא, in the name of רבא, starts a statement: for the first clause of the משנה as well, one should not bring a certain proof. The rest of the statement comes after this text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא, the father of רב הונא בר תחליפא, said in the name of רבא: the first clause also, do not bring it from…
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins about the first clause of the משנה. The sentence is not finished here, so the גמרא is setting up a point that is completed right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first clause' is the משנה's rule that people who owe a חטאת or a definite אשם must still bring it after יום הכפורים. רבא is saying that this clause also should not be derived in a certain way. His full point continues past the end of this text.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one, meaning the first clause of the משנה
Do not bring it (from here), meaning this source does not prove it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא
phrases.english: Rav Tahlifa, father of Rav Huna bar Tahlifa, said
in the name of Rava:
the first clause as well, do not bring [a proof]
phrases.notes: The first clause is the משנה's rule that a חטאת or definite אשם must still be brought after יום הכפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the אשם תלוי clause back to the משנה's first clause
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא holds that the first clause of the משנה also should not be derived in a certain way. The full statement continues after this text.
